prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (2015 manifesto)

Public finances and tax
- Eliminate the structural current budget deficit by 2017/18; have debt fall as a share of GDP; introduce two fiscal rules allowing borrowing for productive investment once day-to-day spending is balanced.
- Fund consolidation via measures on high earners, banks, large firms and polluters; no increases to headline Income Tax, National Insurance, VAT or Corporation Tax rates.
- Raise the Personal Allowance to at least £12,500; consider aligning the employee NI threshold; clamp down on avoidance/evasion; introduce a high-value property levy (over £2m).

Economy, innovation and skills
- Expand the Industrial Strategy; aim to double economy-wide R&D; protect and grow science budgets; extend Catapult centres.
- Strengthen the British Business Bank; promote alternative finance and community banking.
- Reform Business Rates and examine Land Value Tax; devolve economic powers to local areas; use procurement to support SMEs.
- Major expansion of high-quality apprenticeships and creation of National Colleges.

Energy, climate and environment
- Zero Carbon Britain Act (net zero by 2050); power-sector decarbonisation target for 2030 (50–100g CO2/kWh); indicative 60% renewables by 2030.
- End unabated coal by 2025; expand CCS, storage and smart grids; support community energy; accept new nuclear without public subsidy and subject to safety/waste controls.
- Use 50% of shale tax revenues for a Low-Carbon Transition Fund; offer finished wells for geothermal reuse.
- Five “green laws” covering nature, zero waste/resource efficiency, green transport, zero-carbon target, and green buildings.
- Nature Act, new National Nature Parks, complete coastal path, plant a tree per child; designate coherent marine protected areas.
- Statutory 70% household recycling target; rebalance landfill/incineration incentives; promote circular-economy design.

Transport and infrastructure
- 10-year rolling capital plans; electrify most rail; proceed with HS2 and key east–west/northern links; shift freight to rail; support light rail.
- National Air Quality Plan with Low Emission Zones; invest in cycling; accelerate ultra-low-emission vehicles and set end-dates for conventional fleets.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS funding in England by at least £8bn a year by 2020; boost mental health funding with access and waiting-time standards.
- Pool health and social care budgets locally by 2018; expand GP access; integrate pharmacy and community services.
- Public health: curb junk food marketing to children, tobacco levy, proportionate e‑cig rules, minimum alcohol pricing.
- Support carers (annual bonus, leave, identification in NHS); complete care-cost cap; improve care workforce standards.

Education and young people
- Protect funding from early years to 19; raise early-years quality and Pupil Premium; ensure qualified teachers in every class.
- Independent standards body; slim core curriculum including PSHE/financial literacy and RE; extend free school meals in primary.
- Double businesses hiring apprentices; expand Higher Apprenticeships; young person’s bus discount card.
- Universities: widen participation, transparency, credit transfer, protect/extend income-contingent loans; review HE finance.

Housing
- Build up to 300,000 homes/year; new Garden Cities and public land release; Housing Investment Bank; planning reforms prioritising brownfield.
- More affordable housing via flexible council borrowing; Rent to Own; Help to Rent deposit loans; stronger tenant protections and licensing.
- Green Buildings Act: lift home efficiency to EPC C by 2035 (fuel-poor by 2027); council tax discount for major upgrades.

Rights, justice and immigration
- Digital Bill of Rights; protect personal privacy; extend FOI to outsourced public services; uphold Human Rights Act.
- Replace Police and Crime Commissioners with Police Boards; Victims’ Bill of Rights; stronger action on domestic/sexual violence.
- Presumption against short custodial sentences; expand rehabilitation, women’s and youth justice reforms.
- Drug policy: end imprisonment for personal possession; divert to treatment; allow medicinal cannabis; strengthen scientific independence.
- Borders: complete entry/exit checks; faster asylum decisions; permit work after six months; separate students from migration stats.

Governance and international
- Devolution to nations and English localities; constitutional convention; votes at 16; proportional voting (STV); Lords reform.
- Remain engaged in EU; deepen single market; back trade deals with safeguards; referendum only on future sovereignty‑shifting treaty change.
- Defence: early SDSR; Single Security Budget; reduce nuclear posture (end continuous patrols); invest in cyber; stronger veteran support.
- Maintain 0.7% aid; drive tax transparency; support global climate agreement and stronger EU targets.
